practicals.title: Case scope and evidence-readiness plan
practicals.scenario: A small organization reports possible misuse of a service account on a synthetic workstation. Learners receive a short intake note and an inventory of possible evidence sources.
practicals.learnerTask: Define the investigative question, authorized scope, lifecycle stages, likely evidence, preservation concerns, and at least one distinction between observation and inference.
expectedReasoning: Keep collection proportionate to the question.
Identify evidence that may change or disappear.
Name assumptions and an alternative explanation before analysis.
practicals.learnerOutput: A bounded case brief, evidence-source matrix, lifecycle sequence, and uncertainty note.
practicals.safetyBoundary: Textual synthetic inputs only; no real identity, endpoint, or incident data.
practicals.limitations: The exercise tests planning and reasoning, not legal advice or collection execution.

practicals.title: Acquisition, integrity, and custody plan
practicals.scenario: The same synthetic case provides a device description, a proposed live/dead collection choice, source and verification digest records, and an incomplete custody form.
practicals.learnerTask: Choose and justify a collection approach, separate original and working copy, complete a synthetic custody record, interpret the digest comparison, and document control limitations.
expectedReasoning: Hash comparison addresses byte identity under its stated scope.
Write protection and custody answer different control questions.
A collection method can change state and must be documented.
practicals.learnerOutput: An acquisition decision record, preservation plan, hash verification record, and Chain-of-Custody worksheet.
practicals.safetyBoundary: No device access, image mounting, command execution, or real evidence handling.
practicals.limitations: The exercise does not certify a legally sufficient form or universal acquisition method.

practicals.title: Filesystem and metadata interpretation
practicals.scenario: A synthetic image inventory contains a partition map, selected filesystem records, an allocated file, a deleted entry, a slack-space fragment, and timestamp metadata with a stated clock offset.
practicals.learnerTask: Explain the storage layers, classify the records, state what the deleted and slack observations do not prove, and produce a bounded interpretation of the NTFS/MFT metadata.
expectedReasoning: Keep layer, record, and interpretation distinct.
Preserve original times and state normalization assumptions.
Require corroboration before inferring ownership, execution, or intent.
practicals.learnerOutput: A filesystem interpretation worksheet with evidence links, timestamp notes, and limitations.
practicals.safetyBoundary: Synthetic metadata cards only; no disk image, filesystem image, or recovery tool is used.
practicals.limitations: NTFS/MFT details remain version-bounded and are not implementation training.

practicals.title: Windows host-artifact correlation
practicals.scenario: A synthetic Windows host packet contains an event-log row, Registry state, a Prefetch-like trace, a shortcut record, and a scheduled backup note.
practicals.learnerTask: Correlate the artifact observations to the question, record OS/parser version assumptions, compare the backup alternative, and draft a cautious finding.
expectedReasoning: Artifact presence is not definitive proof of user action.
Independent sources and configuration context affect interpretation.
Version and retention gaps remain visible.
practicals.learnerOutput: An artifact-correlation matrix, alternative-explanation note, and bounded finding draft.
practicals.safetyBoundary: No Windows host, Registry hive, browser history, or user data is collected.
practicals.limitations: Artifact schemas and behavior require revalidation for a selected OS version before any future update.

practicals.title: Volatile-data triage interpretation
practicals.scenario: A synthetic memory-triage packet describes a process tree, a network endpoint, a loaded module, collection timing, and a parser limitation.
practicals.learnerTask: Set triage priorities, interpret the process/connection/module observations, record acquisition effects and authorization questions, and identify corroborating sources.
expectedReasoning: Collection can change the system state.
A process or module observation is a lead, not a verdict.
Potential secrets are sensitive and outside this exercise’s data.
practicals.learnerOutput: A bounded triage plan, observation/inference table, and corroboration request list.
practicals.safetyBoundary: No memory dump, credential material, malware, or live system is used.
practicals.limitations: The specification does not teach memory acquisition commands or secret extraction.

practicals.title: Network and log timeline construction
practicals.scenario: The synthetic case adds DNS, HTTP metadata, authentication events, endpoint observations, and a proxy retention gap from three clocks.
practicals.learnerTask: Preserve original timestamps, normalize the views, build a timeline, connect events only where justified, and mark conflicts and gaps.
expectedReasoning: Timezone conversion does not prove clock accuracy.
Network visibility is partial and source-specific.
A missing proxy record is an uncertainty, not evidence of no transfer.
practicals.learnerOutput: A source-linked timeline, normalization ledger, and gap/conflict analysis.
practicals.safetyBoundary: Synthetic records only; no packet capture, target, network scan, or live collection.
practicals.limitations: The timeline is an analytical exercise and not a reconstruction of a real incident.

practicals.title: Hypothesis and alternative-explanation analysis
practicals.scenario: Learners receive the accumulated synthetic case observations plus two indicators and a benign administrative explanation that fits part of the sequence.
practicals.learnerTask: State a leading hypothesis and alternatives, map supporting and contradictory evidence, identify additional evidence needed, and write a qualitative confidence assessment.
expectedReasoning: A hypothesis is testable and revisable.
Indicators need independent validation.
Confidence should reflect corroboration and gaps, not a made-up number.
practicals.learnerOutput: A hypothesis matrix, IOC validation plan, alternative-explanation analysis, and confidence/limitation note.
practicals.safetyBoundary: All indicators and explanations are synthetic; no malware, credentials, or operational evasion steps.
practicals.limitations: The exercise does not attribute real actors or establish legal conclusions.

practicals.title: Integrated synthetic investigation and report
practicals.scenario: The full synthetic case packet combines the earlier filesystem, host, memory, network, log, timeline, and hypothesis outputs, including a known limitation.
practicals.learnerTask: Validate the case scope and evidence links, reconcile the timeline, select bounded findings, document alternatives and uncertainty, and plan both technical and executive reports.
expectedReasoning: A finding must link observations, analysis, alternatives, and limitations.
Technical detail and executive communication serve different readers.
Reproducibility requires methods, transformations, assumptions, and tool/version notes where relevant.
practicals.learnerOutput: A case validation checklist, finding register, technical report outline, executive summary outline, and residual-gap list.
practicals.safetyBoundary: Textual synthetic specifications only; no source files, real incidents, personal data, malware, or deployment.
practicals.limitations: The capstone remains SPEC_ONLY and has no automated grader or runtime registration.
